entities.summary:
Jean Fonteneau, dit Alfonse de Saintonge or João Afonso in Portuguese was a Portuguese navigator, explorer and corsair, prominent in the European Age of Discovery. He had an early career in Portugal and later served the King of France.

Born in the late 15th century, Alfonse de Saintonge was a key figure in the Portuguese Age of Exploration, which aimed to establish a vast maritime empire that would rival the Ottoman Empire.

Alfonse's most notable achievement was his participation in the ill-fated voyage of Pedro Álvares Cabral, who discovered Brazil in 1500. Alfonse's navigational skills and bravery were crucial to the success of this voyage, which marked the beginning of European exploration and colonization in the Americas.

As a corsair, Alfonse de Saintonge also played a significant role in the struggle for power between Portugal and France. He worked closely with the French monarchy to disrupt Spanish shipping and secure French dominance in the Atlantic.

Alfonse's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his exploits helped shape the course of European history. The Age of Exploration, which he played a part in, had far-reaching consequences for the development of globalization, imperialism, and the modern nation-state.

One of the most striking aspects of Alfonse's life is the irony that he, a Frenchman, played a pivotal role in the Portuguese Age of Exploration, which had a profound impact on the history of France and the world.
